answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so memory_b1 and memory_b6 (both about release gating/rollback) cannot drive the action no matter how well they worked before. Regional failover (memory_b2) moved traffic cleanly during a latency degradation, but that incident was regional/network-shaped; here the symptom is write-path saturation at peak settlement volume, and shifting a write-heavy peak across regions risks in-flight write loss, which directly violates the 'without losing customer writes' constraint. Adding capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned BEFORE a known peak; mid-incident provisioning rarely lands in time and does nothing for 90 minutes of already-accumulated pressure. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained an external partner outage by failing fast \u2014 but the fault here appears internal, and failing fast on our own write path means shedding customer writes, again against the stated objective. That leaves read-replica routing (memory_b5): taking dashboard/report load off the primary is the only candidate that reduces primary contention without touching the write path or the patched build, and it is reversible. Note the actual causal claim in memory_b5 is thin \u2014 it reports that write latency 'recovered the same day' after replica routing, which is correlational and came from a reporting-load-driven incident, not a settlement-peak write surge. Whether report queries are a material share of current primary load is exactly the unknown, so I am spending my one verification on memory_b5 to check the original record for the load breakdown and whether write latency recovery was attributed to the routing change or coincided with the load window ending. Downstream value risk: replicas serve stale reads, so settlement dashboards and any reconciliation or risk decisions consuming them will silently operate on lagged data during peak \u2014 that staleness must be surfaced to finance/ops rather than left implicit, or we trade an availability win for bad money decisions. Scoping as a small guarded test: shift a bounded slice of report traffic first with replica lag and primary contention as explicit kill-criteria, expanding only if primary p99 actually responds. If it does not move within a short window, that falsifies the memory_b5 mechanism here and the next window should go to failover or capacity rather than more replica routing.
